text:
maria_ops: Heads up — BrightDocs escalation incoming. Customer reports intermittent 502/504s on hosted API since ~09:22 UTC, p95 > 10s for some endpoints. Tenant: t-bright-42. They attached SDK logs and a short repro.
aj_oncall: On it. I see alerts from the gateway. @sre_bot can you paste the alert summary?
sre_bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway queue_depth exceeded threshold on region-us-west-2 for tenant t-bright-42. 5xx_rate elevated to 12% above baseline. See https://alerts.redwood/INC-3456
kim_support: Customer repro note: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-bright' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> 504 after ~12s. They also saw 401s earlier today then timeouts.
lee_customer: Customer says their billing email bounced yesterday and card failed. They saw a few 401s from the API, then their app retried aggressively (no jitter). "We started seeing timeouts after that, entire integration became flaky."
devin_infra: Hypothesis: transient auth failures -> aggressive client retries -> concentrated request bursts hitting the same prefix -> continuous batching backlog and KV-cache churn -> queue depth exhaustion -> tail-latency 5xx/timeouts. We can repro with a scripted retry loop.
maria_ops: Trace sample (trimmed):
```
gateway: queued_request_count=384
batcher: assemble_latency=1.8s
kvcache: backend_load_timeout=5s
```
aj_oncall: billing_bot, did the tenant get suspended for non-payment? that could explain 401s turning on/off.
billing_bot: NOTE: Invoice INV-20260314-894 failed for org brightdocs on 2026-03-14 02:11:23 UTC. Auto-suspend policy = 'notify' (no auto-suspend). Account remained active. Payment issue present.
kim_support: So not an account suspension. Likely transient auth errors (token rotation or gateway auth hiccup) combined with client retry amplification.
devin_infra: Immediate mitigations I recommend:
- Per-tenant inflight cap -> cap queued requests for t-bright-42 to 50.
- Route tenant to smaller model fallback (gpt-lite) to reduce assembly time while we stabilize.
- Patch gateway to respect Retry-After and enforce retry rate limits for 401/5xx responses.
aj_oncall: Applying targeted throttle now and enabling fallback route. Also flipping on prefix dedupe bypass to avoid repeated heavy KV loads for identical immediate retries.
maria_ops: Customer-facing message drafted: explain transient auth + retry amplification caused tail timeouts; we've throttled and routed to fallback, monitoring p95. Will follow up when stable.
lee_customer: Customer accepted temporary fallback. They want repro steps to validate fix on their side.
aj_oncall: Internal repro steps to validate:
1) Run ~200 concurrent clients hitting /v1/generate with a token that returns 401 for ~20% of requests.
2) No backoff: immediate retry 3x.
3) Observe gateway.queue_depth and batcher assemble times over 30s.
Quick curl snippet (internal only):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer BROKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
```
Expected: queue_depth > 300, p95 latency > 8s, 5xx spikes.
devin_infra: Long-term fixes:
- SDK guidance: exponential backoff + jitter and honor Retry-After on 401/429.
- Auth service: differentiate transient auth errors vs credential invalid, consider 429 for rate-limiting cases.
- Gateway: per-tenant circuit breaker that fails fast before allowing queue saturation.
- KV-cache improvements: bypass hot-path for immediate retries within 200ms window.
kim_support: Action items:
- aj_oncall: throttle & fallback (prod) — in progress
- devin_infra: KV-cache bypass PR (#1453) + retry-rate-limit patch
- maria_ops: customer update + postmortem draft
- billing_team (cc): improve notification delivery for payment issues to reduce customer-side retry loops
maria_ops: Update: throttle applied and fallback enabled. Within ~3m p95 dropped to 430ms and 5xxs down to ~1.2%. Leaving fallback on until 15:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
sre_bot: RESOLVED: hosted-gateway queue_depth normalized for t-bright-42. Incident mitigated. Recommend full postmortem and SDK update to prevent recurrence.
